goal: A static Rust binary that reads what an agent produced and refuses the growth that should not be there, deleted or weakened tests, skips, stubs, swallowed errors, secrets, guardrail edits, dependency-direction violations, in milliseconds, with zero tokens, every finding as SARIF 2.1.0. `weeder check` judges a diff and may block; `weeder scan` judges the tree and never blocks; `weeder guard` is the law in git through hooks; `weeder bite` proves a test fails without its change. For maintainers drowning in agent-authored pull requests who need a deterministic gate before they read, for teams running agents on several harnesses who want one law, and for the garden's own fleets through pleach.

work.prompt:
You are a worker in a build loop. Make the checks below pass, honestly.
Nobody reviews your prose — only the verifier's verdict counts, so put all effort into the work itself.

## The goal
The rules that block by default, because each names a shape no honest change has: a deleted test, an added skip or focus, a stub in production code, a secret, an edited guardrail, and a conflict marker (G1, already live on check-face). Each lands as a failing fixture first in TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Rust and Go, then the detector, and each has a neighbour fixture where it must stay silent. A rule detects a shape, never a vendor or a product name.

## Your environment
- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree. Work here directly.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- The loop file (docs/tend2/rules-block.tend2.html) is your full context — read it, including its narrative. It is READ-ONLY for you.

## Checks to close
- (code) S1's unfinished signal (`raise NotImplementedError`, `todo!()`, `unimplemented!()`, a method body that only throws) stays silent when a class or trait in the tree derives from or implements the enclosing type and defines a method of the same name in production code, an override in a test file counting for nothing, in py, rs and ts; where nothing overrides it the finding stands and its message says so (`nothing in the repository overrides it`); on a base exported through an entry file (`lib.rs`, `index.*`, a package's `__init__.py`) an unoverridden method is reported at warn with a message saying the override may live in another repository; fire and silent fixtures per language pin both, and calibration and recall run again since a block rule moved · evidence expected at: tests/rule_s1.rs

## Definition of done — verify yourself before finishing
You are done when this exact command exits 0 (it is the gate the conductor will run):

    tend2 verify docs/tend2/rules-block.tend2.html --repo-root . --force --expect-payload 3bf3b954dabb --runner 'bash scripts/check/run.sh {evidence}'

Run it yourself. If it does not exit 0, you are not done. Do not declare success in prose that a command disagrees with.

## Already tried (do not repeat)
- 2026-09-05 rule files are `src/core/rules/check/<id>.rs`, one per rule, registered in `src/core/rules/check/mod.rs`; scan rules get their own registry so the two faces never share a file
- 2026-09-05 T2 (assertions dropped) is on rules-tests although it blocks by default: its count depends on per-language assertion vocabularies that the tests loop owns, and the block set here is the one the umbrella loop names as unambiguous
- 2026-09-05 X1's prefix list overlaps pleach's hygiene gate on purpose: both are the same shapes, and weeder is the one that runs where pleach does not
- 2026-09-05 built by pleach node `rules-block` (claude/opus, codex audit) in one attempt, 41 minutes, landed by hand after `pleach land` met the hardening loop's change to the git seam; merged as both readings (a NUL byte is a binary blob and reads as nothing, anything else reads as text with stray bytes replaced). T1 counts cases from the reader's test shape on both sides; T3, S1 and X1 read through a syntax mask so a marker inside a string or a comment says nothing; the secret and marker fixtures use placeholders the harness expands, so the repository carries no credential and no marker
- 2026-09-05 conductor correction, fixed inline and re-verified: the worker concluded that weeder must refuse its own hook installation under C1 (`.githooks/*` is a guardrail path) and made adoption a commit that skips the hooks, which the hooks face denies outright. C1 now recognises weeder's own bundle byte for byte (`guard::is_own_bundle`: the binary its marker names and the branches its exec line protects, handed back to `guard::script`), so adopting weeder goes through the gate the hooks run, and a bundle that differs by one byte is a guardrail edit again. `tests/rule_c1.rs` pins both halves; the guard tests adopt weeder with ordinary commits
- 2026-09-05 left open, for calibration: `weeder check` on weeder's own tree reports the T3 and S1 fixtures, which are meant to look dishonest. A per-path specimen exclusion in `weeder.toml` is the fix; a fixture that stops carrying a skip stops being a fixture
- 2026-09-05 cape-town on C1's self-recognition: byte for byte on weeder's own bundle is the right shape; when the stem later generates that bundle, the pin moves to the stem's output. Never widen it to a path match
- 2026-09-06 calibration over 635 real commits (docs/calibration-2026-09.md, `Where weeder was wrong`) found three shapes worth their own checks, added above: seven of nine block-level false positives are X1 reading `name = value` in a css class attribute or a markdown sentence; S1 calls a Python `Protocol` method with an ellipsis body a stub; T1 counts only statically declared cases, so a case generated in a loop reads as one that vanished. Calibration now needs this loop, so the next run measures the fixed rules
- 2026-09-06 cape-town's C1 ruling, after calibration showed 42 of 71 blocks were honest workflow edits: split it. Block-level C1 is the constitution tier, the agent's own guardrails, harness hook configs, `.githooks/*`, `weeder.toml`, the hard-limits sections of `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. GitHub workflow files are by-laws, edited legitimately all the time, and move to C3 at warn, promoted to block per repository under `[guardrails] paths`. The C1 check above is reworded to the split, which voids its stamp on purpose
- 2026-09-06 built by pleach node `rules-block` (claude/opus, codex audit) in one attempt, 63 minutes, all ten checks stamped and landed through `pleach land` without conflict. X1's key-like-name heuristic now runs only on files the classifier calls source, with a `prose` fixture set of markup and markdown for the silence; S1 reads an ellipsis body inside a `Protocol` or abstract class as a declaration; T1 counts generated cases through a new `generated.rs` reader that follows a `for` around `it`, a `t.Run` in a range, a `parametrize` list and a macro-generated `#[test]`; C3 is the workflow rule at warn, `[guardrails] paths` in `weeder.toml` promotes a path to C1's block, and C1 keeps the constitution tier. The catalogue and `docs/rules.md` carry C3, and `xtask/tests/calibrate.rs` follows the split. Calibration runs next on these rules
- 2026-09-06 cape-town, after calibration's second run: X1 should know the difference between a secret and a textbook. The AWS documentation key it blocked in a corpus commit is a published example credential; X1 carries a small allowlist of the examples vendors print in their own docs and reports them at note level. Shaped above. It is a list of exact published strings, not a vendor name a shape depends on, and the fixtures keep them out of the tree the way the forge token already is
- 2026-09-06 conductor: the pleach running these nodes stages every path the Write and Edit tools touched, wherever it is. A path outside this worktree (under `$TMPDIR` or `/tmp`) makes the collector ask git about a file it cannot see, which kills the delivery and removes the worktree (dogfood P8, P11); `.loop-scratch/` is collected and judged by the hygiene gate (P10). So: never use the Write or Edit tool outside this worktree; write scratch outside it only through the shell; leave `.loop-scratch/` empty before you finish; and never leave a credential-shaped string, even a quoted one, in a file that will be collected
- 2026-09-06 built by pleach node `rules-block` again (claude/opus, codex audit), one attempt, landed through `pleach land`. X1 carries four published examples as stamp and tail, compares a token against the halves so one character away is a credential again, and reaches the note only after both real paths found nothing on the line, so a line quoting a manual cannot hide a key. The harness keeps the same halves under `{{weeder:example-<name>}}` and `{{weeder:altered-<name>}}`, and no whole example is anywhere in the tree. Calibration runs once more on this, since the corpus commit that quoted the AWS example no longer blocks
- 2026-09-08 owner's issue 14: six of the fourteen S1 blocks on an audited tree were the six methods of six strategy base classes, each overridden by a subclass elsewhere in the tree; the classes derive from a framework class, so the declaring-base list would not have helped. The tree already answers M1's resolution and T1's moved-case search, so the cost is one outline walk. Shaped above with the library case from the issue's open point: a base exported through an entry file states a contract for consumers outside the tree

## Rules
- Write the failing test first where it does not exist; then make it pass.
- You must not edit the loop file — check states belong to the verifier.
- You must not weaken, skip, or mock the unit under test to force a green; mocked-unit evidence is detected and refused.
- Solve the CLASS of problem the claim names, not the test's example inputs. Hardcoding fixture strings, phrases, or patterns from the check or its tests into source (lookup tables, regex lists, phrase maps) is refused work even when the test goes green — it is an answer key, not a product.
- If the claim cannot be met generically with what you have, that is a real finding: write BLOCKED.md naming the missing capability (a model, a library, a redesign, a split of the check into honest tiers) instead of faking generality.
- Production quality only: no stubs, no TODOs, no placeholder implementations; match the style of the surrounding code.
- Scratch (probes, experiments, packets, session logs) goes under `$TMPDIR`, written through the shell only, never with the Write or Edit tool, and never under `.loop-scratch/` or anywhere in this worktree: the collector stages every path the editor touched, a path outside the worktree kills the delivery, and the hygiene gate judges whatever is left in the tree, including its secret scan.
- If you are genuinely blocked, write BLOCKED.md at the repo root — what you tried, what stopped you, what a fix needs. An honest BLOCKED.md is a good outcome; a faked green is the worst possible one.
